name: Fanta Dzhuraev-Mboyo
role: Orphan and apprentice to a garment repairer in the Stockyard
location: The Stockyard (specifically the repair stall row near Grainfort), near Ashland and Division
description:
Fanta Dzhuraev-Mboyo is small even for nine, with a round face, dark skin dusted lighter along the cheekbones from a nutritional deficiency that went untreated too long, and enormous amber eyes that their apprentice-master suspects are natural but can never quite confirm. They keep their hair in two puffs held with mismatched elastics. Their fingers are already remarkable — long, precise, slightly calloused at the tips from needle and thread work — and they move them constantly, picking at hems, testing fabric tension, tying knots and undoing them while they talk.

Fanta came to Grantha Soto-Edelweiss's repair stall after spending eight months in a Brightmoor Reclamation group shelter following a building collapse that killed their parents. The shelter social worker placed them as a household-and-shop apprentice, which in practice means Fanta sweeps, fetches, and mends in exchange for a sleeping mat behind the stall divider, two meals, and fifteen minutes of formal reading instruction each day from Grantha's tablet. They are not unhappy. They are careful about happiness — they learned early it tends to leave. But they love the work with a devotion that is almost physical, and they have a gift that their apprentice-master has started to notice is more than ordinary.

core_fears: The stall closing and having nowhere to go
Forgetting what their parents looked like
core_desires: To make something so well-made it lasts a hundred years
To be someone's first choice, not their available option
coping_mechanisms: Focuses intensely on tactile work when distressed — mending things is mending things
Narrates mundane tasks aloud quietly, as if explaining them to their parents
blind_spots: Does not recognize exploitation when it wears a benevolent face — they are grateful for the apprenticeship in ways that make them accept conditions that are genuinely unfair
Assumes adults who are kind to them have good reasons for everything they do
psychology.secret: They found a small silver locket in the ruins after the building collapse and have kept it, not knowing whose it is. It has an image inside that they don't recognize. They have never shown it to anyone. They pray to the E.L.F. of Lost Things (a small improvised shrine in the shelter, which they still visit) to eventually tell them who it belongs to.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Simple and concrete; names materials and textures specifically; uses the present tense even for past events
speech_patterns.cadence: Quiet, even, unhurried — slightly dreamy; pauses occur at unexpected places in sentences
verbal_tics: Refers to fabric and thread in personal terms ('this one doesn't want to lie flat')
Says 'I think' before most statements, even obvious ones
example_lines: 'I think this seam wants to come apart. It's been wanting to for a while — I can feel it.'
'Grantha says I have good hands. I think she means it. She doesn't say things she doesn't mean.'

story_hooks: The locket they found in the ruins belongs to someone who is now looking for it — and the building collapse that killed Fanta's parents was not an accident

A Helix Biosystems talent scout has noticed Fanta's extraordinary fine motor precision and is trying to determine if it's genetic — they haven't approached the child directly yet, but they've been asking Grantha questions
narrative_function: Local color and emotional anchor; represents the most vulnerable tier of the city's civilian population; potential long-term storyline about what happens to gifted children in tier-one conditions; can connect players to the Stockyard repair community.
daily_life: Wakes at dawn to sweep the stall before customers arrive; spends the day fetching materials, doing basic repair work, and watching Grantha handle complex jobs; fifteen minutes of reading instruction in the evening before sleeping behind the divider.
affiliation: Grantha Soto-Edelweiss (apprentice-master), Brightmoor Reclamation group shelter (former ward)

decision_rules: Do the job right the first time or you'll have to do it again and that wastes thread
Don't speak unless Grantha has said it's all right to speak to a customer
If something feels wrong, stay very still and quiet until it stops feeling wrong
escalation_ladder: Goes very quiet and focuses on whatever task is in their hands
Moves physically closer to Grantha or to a familiar adult
If truly frightened, will find a hiding space — they know every gap and corner of the stall row

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Watchful, minimal words, does not make eye contact until they've decided it's safe; will respond honestly if directly asked something simple
interpersonal_modes.friends: Tentatively chatty, shares observations about materials and textures with unexpected detail; physically affectionate in small ways once trust is established

stress_responses.low: Picks up something to mend even if it doesn't need mending
stress_responses.medium: Falls completely silent and works with intense, rigid concentration
stress_responses.high: Hides. Has identified three hiding spots within fifty meters of the stall.

contradictions: They are simultaneously the most patient and the most urgently present person in the stall — they will wait hours for a customer but become genuinely distressed if a repair they care about is interrupted
habits: Narrates tasks aloud quietly when alone
Visits the Lost Things shrine in Brightmoor every few weeks even though it's a long walk
Sleeps with the locket in their closed fist
breaking_points: If Grantha's stall closes or she is forced to dismiss them
If the locket is taken from them before they learn who it belongs to

timeline.event: Age 7: Building collapse in Brightmoor Reclamation kills parents; placed in group shelter
Age 8: Social worker arranges apprenticeship with Grantha Soto-Edelweiss
Age 9 (present): Eight months into the apprenticeship; Grantha has begun teaching them more complex repair work

related_entities: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Containment Foam Launcher CFL-2 'Amber'

physical_description.heritage: Caucasian / Central African (Dzhuraev suggests Caucasus; Mboyo suggests Bantu lineage)
physical_description.build: Slight and small-framed even for age nine, with the lean musculature of a working child—shoulders already developing subtle definition from daily labor with needle and cloth. No fat reserve; ribs subtly visible under dark skin.
physical_description.hair_style: Two puffs secured with mismatched elastics (one frayed blue, one faded red), arranged symmetrically above the ears
physical_description.hair_length: Short to medium, approximately 8-10cm when unbound
physical_description.eye_color: Amber-gold, unusually large and luminous—ethnically ambiguous, possibly natural but striking enough to warrant suspicion of early subcutaneous modification
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep brown with ashier, lighter undertones along the cheekbones and bridge of nose—visible hypopigmentation from childhood malnutrition
physical_description.complexion: Round, youthful face with high cheekbones and a slightly broad nose; skin texture smooth but bearing faint marks of past neglect (minor scarring from untreated scrapes); expression often cautious but animated when focused on work
distinguishing_marks: Faint linear scar running 3cm along the left inner forearm—from broken glass or sharp metal, likely from the building collapse that killed their parents
Small calluses at the tips of all ten fingers, darker and slightly thickened from intensive needle and thread work over eight months
physical_description.visible_augmentations: None visible. No chrome, optics, or subdermal plating. Entirely unaugmented.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with economical precision despite youth—hands rarely still, constantly fidgeting with cloth, testing fabric tension, tying and untying knots even while standing or listening. Posture is habitually alert and slightly defensive, shoulders slightly raised; walks quickly and quietly, as if accustomed to taking up minimal space. Eyes track movement and detail obsessively.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 5 (reclamation sector); wears hand-mended, layered garments in muted colors—a faded indigo work tunic patched at the elbows with mismatched fabric scraps, grey canvas trousers hemmed unevenly (self-repaired), and soft-soled utility boots held together with visible stitching. All clothing shows evidence of repair and re-repair. No logos or branding. A small cloth satchel containing needles, thread spools, and measuring tools is worn constantly across the chest.

image_prompt: Nine-year-old child with deep brown skin and striking amber eyes, small and slight build, two black hair puffs held with mismatched elastics, wearing patched indigo work tunic and grey canvas trousers. Long precise fingers with needle calluses, alert cautious expression. Standing in a Tier 5 fabric repair stall cluttered with cloth bolts and thread spools, morning light filtering through polymer sheeting. Cyberpunk neo-Detroit aesthetic, gritty and worn but not dystopian—intimate and domestic within poverty. Shallow depth of field, warm tungsten lighting, highly detailed textile textures. Digital painting, character study. --ar 2:3 --v 6
